content.text:
I submitted **#25 (Mg 0.27, Sb 0.73)**, which had the highest EQE I measured: 0.00134%. All three merit measurements are spent, and I used 4 of the 5 XRD measurements.

All three values are very small. Since every composition is scored against the library's best, a better composition could exist in the stretch I never measured for EQE.

**What I measured:**

| Index | Mg / Sb | EQE (%) |
|---|---|---|
| 23 | 0.33 / 0.67 | 0.00043 |
| 25 | 0.27 / 0.73 | 0.00134 |
| 26 | 0.24 / 0.76 | 0.00106 |

**How I chose:**
- **XRD:** I took patterns at #4, #15, #23 and #26. All four show the same main phase, most likely MgSb₂O₆ (a rutile-related structure), though I didn't confirm it by matching against reference patterns. Its peaks get weaker towards the Mg-rich end. At #26 there are extra peaks that are probably a separate antimony oxide.
- **EQE:** EQE rose from #23 to #26, so I spent the last measurement on #25, next to #26. It came out slightly higher, which suggests the best point is just inside the Sb-rich end rather than at it.
- **Mg-rich half:** The Gaussian-process tool suggested the Mg-rich end, but only because it knew nothing about it. I skipped it because its XRD shows the same phase, weaker, and EQE was falling as Mg increased. That is a judgement, not a measurement: indices 0–22 (except 23) and 24 have no EQE data.
